findings.claim: src/ui/finish-panel.ts has been dead since B02 (#10): no file in src/ imports it, because createRaceUi shows the results screen instead. Only two existing tests keep it alive, and they test a screen the player never sees. Its CSS rules (.ui-finish__card/__stats/__stat) are dead along with it.
findings.evidence: grep `finish-panel|FinishPanel` in src/ returns only src/ui/finish-panel.ts:10,21,25 (its own declarations). Importers: tests/ui/screens.test.ts:3 `import { createFinishPanel } from '../../src/ui/finish-panel.ts'` (used at :11 and :45, asserting 'Race again' and 'Finished'), and tests/ui/no-inline-colour.test.ts:6 (used at :25). The dead CSS is src/ui/screens.css:62-81 (`.ui-finish__card`, `.ui-finish__stats`, `.ui-finish__stat`), which only finish-panel.ts:31-42 uses.
findings.suggestedFix: Owner: remove the finish-panel cases from screens.test.ts (keep the start-screen ones) and the createFinishPanel line from no-inline-colour.test.ts, which is better replaced by the pause/results coverage in the separate tests finding. Then delete src/ui/finish-panel.ts and screens.css:62-81.

findings.claim: The results screen's root still carries the legacy `ui-finish` class only so that old finish-panel tests keep finding it. No CSS rule targets `.ui-finish` on its own. Tests should find the results screen by role or text, not by this leftover class.
findings.evidence: src/ui/results-screen.ts:64 `'ui-results ui-finish',`. In src, `ui-finish` otherwise appears only as `.ui-finish__*` in finish-panel.ts and screens.css:63-81. Pinned by tests/ui/race-ui.test.ts:16 `finish: () => q('.ui-finish')` (test title :47 'shows the finish panel once') and tests/ui/results-screen.test.ts:34 `expect(el.classList.contains('ui-finish')).toBe(true)`.
findings.suggestedFix: Owner: make race-ui.test.ts look the screen up through `[role="table"][aria-label="Results"]` (or `.ui-results`) and drop the assertion at results-screen.test.ts:34. Then drop ` ui-finish` from results-screen.ts:64, together with the finish-panel removal.

findings.claim: The 'no colour in any inline style or SVG paint attribute' rule is never checked for the pause screen. The results screen gets only a weaker check: 4 paint attributes instead of 7, and it does not allow hatch url() fills. Both screens use icons and the hatch, which is exactly where a stray fill/stroke attribute would slip in.
findings.evidence: tests/ui/no-inline-colour.test.ts:19-25 builds the HUD, touch controls, countdown, start screen and the dead finish panel, but not createPauseScreen (src/ui/pause-screen.ts:27) or the results screen. tests/ui/results-screen.test.ts:120-126 checks only `['fill','stroke','color','stop-color']`, while PAINT_ATTRS in no-inline-colour.test.ts:14 also has flood-color, lighting-color and bgcolor. No test checks inline colour on .ui-pause (grep COLOUR_PROPS: only those two files).
findings.suggestedFix: Add a new test file. It renders createPauseScreen(...).show({lap:1,laps:3,timeMs:0}) and a createRaceUi synced to a finished RaceView (results visible). It then applies the same COLOUR_PROPS/COLOUR_VALUE/PAINT_ATTRS checks as no-inline-colour.test.ts, allowing only `url(#…)` paint references. It passes on main today: icons.ts and the hatch set no colour attributes.

findings.claim: Game tests copy the same harness again and again: a hand-driven requestAnimationFrame stub with runFrames, setup(), esc(), the render mock, and the 'bot drives car 0 of a twin world' input recorder. The recorder is already shared as twinPlayerInputs in tests/game/helpers.ts. The render mocks also still stub `playerLivery`, which game.ts no longer imports.
findings.evidence: runFrames is identical in pause.test.ts:41-48, pause-review.test.ts:39-46 and pause-results.test.ts:36-43, along with the rAF/cAF stubs at :27-30, :25-28 and :24-27. esc() is copied at pause.test.ts:57 and pause-results.test.ts:70. The twin-world recorders pause-results.test.ts:57-68 `winningInputs()` and results-drivers.test.ts:23-33 `playerInputs()` duplicate tests/game/helpers.ts:9-20 `twinPlayerInputs(trackId, seed, carCount, maxTicks)` (same loop, 2 cars, 60*60*10 ticks). Stale mock entries: `playerLivery: (n) => …` at pause.test.ts:14, pause-review.test.ts:13, pause-results.test.ts:12 and start-race-invalid-count.test.ts:10, while tests/content/drivers.test.ts:80 asserts game.ts does not mention playerLivery.
findings.suggestedFix: Owner: move runFrames, the rAF stub install and esc() into tests/game/helpers.ts (or a new tests/game/frames.ts). Replace winningInputs/playerInputs with twinPlayerInputs(TRACK, SEED, 2, 36000), and drop the playerLivery mock lines. vi.mock must stay in each file because it is hoisted per module.

findings.claim: The RacerView/RaceView/CarView fixture builders are copied word for word into five test files, while tests/ui/helpers.ts already holds the shared hudState/outline fixtures and tests/render/helpers.ts:21 has an equivalent carView(). If RacerView gains a required field, a feature night has to touch five append-only files it cannot edit.
findings.evidence: `const racer = (over: Partial<RacerView> = {}): RacerView => ({ lapsCompleted: 0, lap: 1, lapTicks: [], finishTick: null, position: 1, ...over });` appears in race-ui.test.ts:8, results-screen.test.ts:9, results-review.test.ts:9, results-drivers.test.ts:9 and pause.test.ts:68. `const finished = (racers) => ({ phase: 'finished', countdown: 0, raceTick: 8000, racers })` appears in results-screen.test.ts:10, results-review.test.ts:10 and results-drivers.test.ts:10. `const car = (x) => ({ x, y: 0, z: 0, heading: 0, pitch: 0, speed: 0, slip: 0, surface: 'dirt', airborne: false })` appears in race-ui.test.ts:7, results-screen.test.ts:8 and pause.test.ts:67, and duplicates tests/render/helpers.ts:21-23 carView().
findings.suggestedFix: Owner: export racerView(over), finishedView(racers) and carAt(x) from tests/ui/helpers.ts, reusing render/helpers carView for the latter. Then replace the local copies with imports.

findings.claim: drivers.test.ts AC5 reads src/game.ts as text and uses a regex to require one exact import statement. It pins how game.ts imports the roster, not what the game does. Any behaviour-preserving refactor of game.ts (splitting it, importing via a content index, aliasing) fails this test.
findings.evidence: tests/content/drivers.test.ts:76-80: `const game = readFileSync('src/game.ts', 'utf8'); expect(game).toMatch(/import \{[^}]*\braceDrivers\b[^}]*\} from '\.\/content\/drivers\.ts'/); expect(game).not.toMatch(/LIVERIES/); expect(game).not.toMatch(/\bbody:\s*'/); expect(game).not.toMatch(/playerLivery/);`. The behaviour it guards (game races use roster liveries) is already covered through the DOM by tests/game/results-drivers.test.ts:48-54 and tests/game/six-car-grid.test.ts.
findings.suggestedFix: Owner: replace the source-text assertions with a behavioural one, such as the started game's state/RaceView driver names or the createRaceScene mock receiving raceDrivers(n) liveries. Or drop them, since results-drivers and six-car-grid already cover it.

findings.claim: The body-into-ground probe clipDepth(world, view) is implemented twice, with slightly different sampling (41 samples vs 81), in two sim tests. tests/sim/helpers.ts is the shared home for such geometry probes (propOverlap, circleOverlap and others).
findings.evidence: tests/sim/ramp-pose.test.ts:13-24 `function clipDepth(world: World, v: CarView): number { const fx = Math.sin(v.heading); const fz = -Math.cos(v.heading); … for (let i = 0; i < SAMPLES; i++) { const t = -1 + (2 * i) / (SAMPLES - 1); …groundAt(world.track, v.x + fx * along, v.z + fz * along).h - body` versus tests/sim/ramp-lip-roll.test.ts:16-26, the same body with `for (let i = 0; i <= 80; i++) { const t = -1 + i / 40;`. Both also redeclare `const HALF = CAR_LENGTH / 2` (:9 and :13).
findings.suggestedFix: Owner: export clipDepth(world, view, samples = 81) from tests/sim/helpers.ts and import it in both files (ramp-pose passes 41).
